title: Vishnu Sahasranamam Lyrics with Meaning: Verses 103-104
desc: Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 103 to 104 in Sanskrit with a simple English meaning and how to chant them: 'प्रमाणं प्राणनिलयः प्राणभृत्प्राणजीवनः'.
alt: Lord Vishnu, Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 103 to 104 with meaning
caption: Vishnu Sahasranamam, verses 103 to 104.
intro: **Vishnu Sahasranamam** is the thousand names of Lord Vishnu, taught by Bhishma to Yudhishthira in the Mahabharata. This post gives **verses 103 to 104** with the Sanskrit text and a plain English meaning, so you can chant with understanding.
takeaways: The verses here open with **प्रमाणं प्राणनिलयः प्राणभृत्प्राणजीवनः**.
Read the Sanskrit slowly, then the meaning, then chant once more.
Thursday and Ekadashi are the days most families keep for Vishnu Sahasranamam.
A short daily portion is better than a rushed full reading.

p: Read the lines aloud, one breath for each half of a verse:
**प्रमाणं प्राणनिलयः प्राणभृत्प्राणजीवनः । तत्त्वं तत्त्वविदेकात्मा जन्ममृत्युजरातिगः ॥** **भूर्भुवःस्वस्तरुस्तारः सविता प्रपितामहः । यज्ञो यज्ञपतिर्यज्वा यज्ञाङ्गो यज्ञवाहनः ॥**

The proof of truth, the dwelling of life, the bearer of life and its very breath is he. The reality, the knower of reality, the one Self, is that God of gods. Beyond birth, death and old age. The tree that holds earth, sky and heaven, the one who carries us across is he. Savita, and the father of the grandfather, is that God of gods. The sacrifice, its lord, the one who performs it, its limbs and its vehicle.
Light a lamp, sit facing east and chant these verses once, then read the meaning silently. Many families take two verses a day and finish the full text in a little under two months.
The names do not need a long ritual. What matters is steady practice, a clear pronunciation and a calm mind.

ul: Thursdays, the day of Vishnu and the planet Jupiter.
Early morning after a bath, or in the evening at the lamp.

faq.q: What do Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 103 to 104 mean?
faq.a: The proof of truth, the dwelling of life, the bearer of life and its very breath is he. The reality, the knower of reality, the one Self, is that God of gods. Beyond birth, death and old age. The tree that holds earth, sky and heaven, the one who carries us across is he. Savita, and the father of the grandfather, is that God of gods. The sacrifice, its lord, the one who performs it, its limbs and its vehicle.
**Bhishma** taught it to Yudhishthira on the field of Kurukshetra, as told in the Anushasana Parva of the Mahabharata.

faq.q: Can I chant a few verses a day instead of the whole text?
faq.a: Yes. A small daily portion with the meaning understood is a common and accepted way to learn it.

note: The Sanskrit is the traditional text. The English is our own plain rendering of the meaning.
